_about: Acronyms on dysnet.org and their full form, shown when the mouse rests on them (or on a tap). build-demo.py writes docs/assets/js/acronyms.js from this file. Add an acronym here when a page starts using it; leave out ambiguous ones (US, OR, IT, EC) and brand names.

acronyms.ACE: angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE inhibitors are blood-pressure medicines)
acronyms.ACOG: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists
acronyms.AEMPS: Agencia Española de Medicamentos y Productos Sanitarios, the Spanish medicines agency
acronyms.AIFA: Agenzia Italiana del Farmaco, the Italian medicines agency
acronyms.AISP: Associazione Italiana Sindrome di Poland, the Italian Poland syndrome association
acronyms.ANSM: Agence nationale de sécurité du médicament et des produits de santé, the French medicines agency
acronyms.ATC: Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical classification of medicines, maintained by the WHO
acronyms.BOND: ERN BOND, the European Reference Network on rare bone diseases
acronyms.CAS: Chemical Abstracts Service registry number, the identifier of a chemical substance
acronyms.CDC: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, United States
acronyms.CHMP: Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use, at the European Medicines Agency
acronyms.CHU: centre hospitalier universitaire, a French university hospital
acronyms.CI: confidence interval: the range within which the true figure most probably lies
acronyms.CLP: Classification, Labelling and Packaging, the EU regulation on hazardous chemicals (Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008)
acronyms.CRAT: Centre de Référence sur les Agents Tératogènes, the French teratology information service in Paris
acronyms.CT: computed tomography, a scan that uses X-rays
acronyms.DNA: deoxyribonucleic acid, the molecule that carries genetic information
acronyms.DOI: digital object identifier, the permanent address of a publication
acronyms.ECLAMC: Estudio Colaborativo Latino Americano de Malformaciones Congénitas, the Latin American collaborative study of congenital malformations
acronyms.ENTIS: European Network of Teratology Information Services
acronyms.EPAR: European public assessment report, the EMA's published evaluation of a medicine
acronyms.ERN: European Reference Network, a network of expert centres for rare diseases
acronyms.EUROCAT: the European network of population-based registries for the surveillance of congenital anomalies
acronyms.EURORDIS: Rare Diseases Europe, the European alliance of rare disease patient organisations
acronyms.FDA: Food and Drug Administration, United States
acronyms.GDPR: General Data Protection Regulation, the EU's data protection law (Regulation (EU) 2016/679)
acronyms.GHS: Globally Harmonized System of Classification and Labelling of Chemicals, of the United Nations
acronyms.HPO: Human Phenotype Ontology, the standard vocabulary of clinical features
acronyms.ICBDSR: International Clearinghouse for Birth Defects Surveillance and Research
acronyms.ICD: International Classification of Diseases, of the WHO
acronyms.ICD-10: International Classification of Diseases, 10th revision, of the WHO
acronyms.ICD-11: International Classification of Diseases, 11th revision, of the WHO
acronyms.ICF: International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health, of the WHO
acronyms.IFSSH: International Federation of Societies for Surgery of the Hand
acronyms.INAIL: Istituto Nazionale Assicurazione contro gli Infortuni sul Lavoro, the Italian national workplace accident insurer
acronyms.INN: International Nonproprietary Name, the generic name the WHO gives a medicine's active substance
acronyms.IRCCS: Istituto di Ricovero e Cura a Carattere Scientifico, an Italian research hospital
acronyms.MHRA: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency, United Kingdom
acronyms.NITE: National Institute of Technology and Evaluation, Japan
acronyms.OMIM: Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man, the catalogue of human genes and genetic disorders
acronyms.OMT: Oberg-Manske-Tonkin classification of congenital hand and upper-limb anomalies
acronyms.ORPHA: ORPHAcode, Orphanet's permanent identifier of a rare disease
acronyms.PRAC: Pharmacovigilance Risk Assessment Committee, at the European Medicines Agency
acronyms.RCP: résumé des caractéristiques du produit, the French summary of product characteristics
acronyms.REACH: Registration, Evaluation, Authorisation and Restriction of Chemicals, the EU chemicals regulation (Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006)
acronyms.SmPC: summary of product characteristics, the official description of a medicine for health professionals
